listBibl.bibl: Felix Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, vol. 1 (Halle: Niemeyer, 1903), p. 529

A semi-literal English rendering of the Latin text, created for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model made by Anthropic. It is a crib to help the reader with the Latin, and should not be treated as a separate translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: Quadr Ded 5
div.ab: Ipsa quippe uitia tanta uirtutibus affinitate coniuncta sunt, ut tarda sit in eis disserendi, iudicandi uel assentiendi nota.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 529 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: For the vices themselves are joined to the virtues by so great an affinity that the mark for discussing, judging or assenting is slow to be found in them.
